slides.heading: Breaking the Chain: Sterilization & Infection Control
slides.subtitle: Cleaning, disinfection, sterilization, isolation, PPE and precautions.

terms.definition: Remove visible dirt with soap & water.

slides.heading: Disinfecting Agents
bullets: Antiseptic (for skin): alcohol (min 60% per CDC), iodine/betadine, chlorhexidine, hydrogen peroxide, silver sulfadiazine.
Disinfectant (non-living surfaces): bleach, quaternary ammonium, phenols, formaldehyde.
Concurrent — while patient is still infectious; Terminal — after patient is gone; Prophylactic — preventive.

terms.definition: Separates people who are sick with a disease (known risk to others).
Separates/restricts people exposed but not yet symptomatic.
Grouping patients with the same infection in an isolated area.

slides.heading: Standard Precautions — Hand Hygiene
bullets: Most effective & practical method to control spread; the key element is FRICTION.
Handwashing: 4 mL liquid soap, 15–20 seconds (if not visibly soiled).
Hand rubbing: 3–5 mL alcohol, 30 seconds of friction.

slides.heading: PPE — Donning & Doffing
bullets: Donning order: Gown → Mask → Goggles → Gloves (GowMaGogGlov).
Doffing order: Gloves → Goggles → Gown → Mask (GlovGogGowMa).
Safe injection: NEVER recap, bend/break, or reuse needles; discard in puncture-resistant containers.

slides.heading: Transmission-Based Precautions
rows: MRSA, VRE, scabies, cutaneous diphtheria, HSV
Surgical mask, single room, spatial separation
N95, negative-pressure room, door closed, 6–12 air changes/hr
Private room, HEPA, positive pressure >12 ACH

slides.heading: Key Takeaways
bullets: Disinfection spares spores; sterilization kills everything.
Autoclave 121–134°C; EtO gas for heat-sensitive items.
Don gown-first, doff gloves-first; hand hygiene's key is friction.
Airborne = N95 + negative pressure; Protective = HEPA + positive pressure.
